questions: Does s-bend progress return to 0.15 or above with the 1 cm pitch, which would confirm that the 2 cm pitch caused the collapse?
Do line_loss_events fall below 1 per run with the denser array?
Is steering_oscillation still within 0.07 to 0.15 with seven sensors, or does the denser array make the signal noisier?
What weight scale did you use for seven sensors at 1 cm pitch, and did kp need changing?
Is rms_error still near 0.03 on all tracks? If so, the offset is probably a motor-mismatch term, and the lever is the controller, not geometry.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If s-bend progress falls below 0.11 with the denser array, the pitch is not the cause, and I will return to the iteration 4 five-sensor layout and test a different variable. If progress is unchanged but line losses stay at 1, tell me whether the line_loss setting (last_direction against search) is the better lever.

intent: Restore the iteration 4 geometry (±3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 16 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius) and change only the sensor pitch, from 1.5 cm (5 sensors) to 1 cm (7 sensors). This tests whether the 2 cm pitch is what collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04 in iterations 2 and 5. Expect s-bend progress at or above 0.155, oval at or above 0.11, and line losses at or below 1 per run.
learning: Iteration 5 (±4 cm, 2 cm pitch, 4 cm lead) collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04 and scored 35.98. The same collapse appeared in iterations 2 and 3, and the good s-bend results (0.155 in iterations 1 and 4) all used a 1.5 cm pitch at ±3 cm. Working hypothesis: pitch of 2 cm or wider breaks the s-bend, so a finer pitch should restore it. Measure s-bend progress, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation on all three development tracks.
rationale: Iteration 5 widened the span to ±4 cm at a 2 cm pitch and scored 35.98, down from 51.12 in iteration 4. The s-bend progress collapsed to 0.04, the same value seen in iterations 2 and 3. The oval (0.115) and slalom (0.1075) were essentially unchanged, and line losses stayed at 1 per run. Four designs have now produced an s-bend of 0.04 and two of them (iterations 2 and 5) used a 2 cm sensor pitch. The best s-bend results (0.155, iterations 1 and 4) both used a 1.5 cm pitch at ±3 cm. Iteration 5 changed both span and pitch, so the collapse cannot be assigned to one variable. The pattern does point at pitch or the wider spacing, not at the 4 cm lead, which is common to the good runs. The cheapest next test is to keep the iteration 4 span (±3 cm) and lead (4 cm), and make the pitch finer. That isolates pitch from span, and it may also give the controller a smoother signal. I therefore propose seven 16 mm sensors at 1 cm pitch across ±3 cm. Iteration 0 used a 1 cm pitch and did not collapse the s-bend (0.15). Body, mass, track and wheel radius stay as in iteration 4, because the off-track limit does not respond to body width within range, and the race is limited by line tracking rather than speed. Expected result: s-bend progress at or above 0.155, oval at or above 0.11, and line losses at or below 1 per run. The Integrator will need to rescale weights for the new pitch.
